newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares mixed to weak in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares mixed to weak in quiet trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares opened the week mixed to weak on continuing profit-taking on Monday with brokers maintaining the bourse would pick up again on high expectations of lower interest rates.
The industrial index -- which last Monday scaled the 7,000 psychological barrier for the first time ever -- dropped 38.41 points to close at 6,714.98.

"We think it's a temporary breather after the bull-run and the market should pick up again because on the macro-economic level the stock exchange is a much more attractive home for investment than the money market," one broker said.
He was referring to a fall in money market rates over the past six months which have driven investors seeking higher yields to the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange.

On the exchange on Monday, merchant banker FMB slid 100 cents to 3,300, tyre manufacturer NTS dropped 50 cents to 450, glass firm PGI shed 30 cents to 490 and tyre manufacturer Dunlop and textiler Spinweave lost 15 cents each to 200 and 140 respectively.
Cable manufacturer BICAF at 390, tea and coffee producer EHPL at 125, building company J and F at 190, tobacco firm TSL at 500, finance group Finhold at 890 all shed 10 cents.

Blue-chip conglomerate Delta and pork processor Colcom traded unchanged in reasonable turnover but industrial holding group IHL surged 550 to 4,200, food group Cairns gained 50 cents to 850, clothing retailer Truworths added five cents to 780 as did multi-industrial group Mash at 135.

Minings were also quiet and easier in light trade with gold producer Falgold dropping 100 cents to 1,700, nickel giant Bindura losing 50 cents to 1,150, Falgold shedding 10 cents to 170 and Wankie Colliery easing five cents down to 350.
The mining index ended 9.68 lower at 1,359.26.
